chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' from al-Husayn ibn Thuwair and Abu Salamah al-Sarraj, they said: We heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

while he was cursing, after every prescribed prayer, four men and four women — al-Taymi, al-Adawi, Fu'lan, and Mu'awiya, and he would name them, and Fu'lanah and Fu'lanah, 'and Hind and Umm al-Hakam, the sister of Mu'awiya'.

key_terms.التَّيْمِيَّ: al-Taymi (referring to Umayr ibn Sa'd al-Taymi)
key_terms.الْعَدَوِيَّ: al-Adawi (referring to Qays ibn Sa'd al-Adawi)

ai.seo_question: Who are the four men and four women cursed by Imam al-Sadiq after prayers?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the practice of *al-Lu'nu* (cursing) by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) after the five daily prayers, specifically targeting key figures from the Umayyad era such as Mu'awiya and Hind bint Utbah. This practice served as a public declaration of *Tawalli* (allegiance to the Ahl al-Bayt) and *Tabarri* (disavowal from their enemies), reinforcing the political and theological stance of the Imams against the ruling caliphs. The inclusion of Hind and Umm al-Hakam underscores the role of prominent women in the early conflicts and their association with the Umayyad lineage.
